title: Astute card
description: One card in the bank: what it asks, what it answers, and the one move it trains. The field names match lib/data/card_json.dart; check.py enforces what a schema cannot say.

id.description: Topic key, a dash, then anything unique. Never reused, even for a retired card.

kind.description: read: turn it over. pickOne: commit to an option. number: work out an exact number. estimate: a Fermi estimate, judged within a factor. debate: take a side, then meet the other one; never graded.

principle.description: What the card is an instance of. Every graded card has one; a read and a debate have none.

answer.description: The reveal. On a number or estimate card it is the last line of the steps.

move.description: The one line that survives the card.

trap.description: The wrong answer most people reach for first, and why it feels right.

hint.description: A way in, without the number.

steps.description: The worked solution, one move per line.

simply.description: A second way in: a concrete image, not the same words made smaller.

counterpoint.description: On a debate, the strongest case against whichever side was taken.

genre.description: One of the six genres under the topic, by id (`space.black_holes`), from lib/data/genres.dart. Every card but a Thinking one has it.

strand.description: One of the three strands under the genre, by id (`space.black_holes.event_horizons`). What a reader would name if asked what they wanted to read about.

keywords.description: Three to six lowercase handles for what the card is about — the things, people, places and ideas in it — for search and for telling two cards apart.

era.description: When the matter is set. `timeless` for a mechanism or a principle; `recent` is the last twenty-five years.

region.description: Where it is set. `none` when the card has no place; `world` when it is everywhere at once.

hook.description: What pulls the reader in: a belief to overturn, a thing to work out, something that happened, a figure that surprises, how it works, two truths that clash, something to use today, where a thing came from.

mood.description: The register the card is read in.

numeracy.description: How much number-sense the card asks for: 0 none, 1 a figure to take in, 2 a comparison or a ratio, 3 a calculation.

abstraction.description: Whether the card is about a thing you can picture, an idea, or one through the other.

shelf_life.description: How soon the claim could go stale: never, in a few years, within the year. Anything but evergreen is re-checked.

mature.description: Sex, drugs, violence, gambling or death in detail. Kept out of a family setting.

language.description: The language the card is written in.

builds_on.description: Ids of cards a reader is better off having met first. The dealer holds this one back until they have, where it can.

figure.description: The picture that would help, if one would, in the vocabulary tool/illustrations can draw.

source.description: The short label the reader sees: institution and document, or the name of the result.

reference.description: Where the claim can be checked: a URL, a DOI, or a book and page. Required on every generated card.

written.description: The day the card was generated.

disabled.description: Retired: never dealt again, still opens in a deck that already holds it.
